title: Walsingham to Edward Wotton, ambassador in Scotland, 28 Jul - 10 Sep 1585, BL Add MS 32657 (DECODE R4838, R4839, R4840, R4844)

steps.what: Fetched DECODE metadata and 18 images of R4838-R4840, R4844 with the saved cookie; also Wotton's drafts R4841-R4843.
Viewed every page: clear English letters with name numbers; only R4844 has sign-alphabet words.
CSP Scotland viii via HathiTrust text view: 28 Jul = no. 40, 7 Aug = no. 65; 21 Aug and 10 Sep not calendared; BHO paywalled.
Name code built from the calendar's bracketed glosses (19, 24, 39, 40), no. 106 (20 = Morton) and sense in Wotton's drafts (10, 11, 36).
Working transcriptions of R4840 and R4844 with numbers glossed.
Looked for Wotton's sign-alphabet key on DECODE and in Tomokiyo's Elizabethan cipher pages; none found.
Looked for cribs to the R4844 sign words; the interlinear decipherment is blotted out and Wotton's drafts carry no sign text. About 120 signs judged too few to break ciphertext-only.

R4840 f. 163 ll. 4-9 re-read on the image for the quotation list (30 Sept): cut after 'towards him' read as 'with the [courage] to procure the practice of 27 and 40, which as he professeth doth greatly [abuse] you, being altogether bent to [ruin] 11 course ... at 3 devotion' (M); old 'overthrow 11' corrected; 28/29/36 glosses not firmed (CSP Scotland viii unreachable, Wotton R4842 has no use of them).

One-key review (Lasry's rule, 14 Oct 2026): the name code and the sign alphabet of 10 Sep are two different ciphers, so the outcome is given per part: name code, key recovered from external plaintext (CSP glosses), 34 of 46 units; sign alphabet not solved, too short. The pooled 0.49 is kept only as a labelled total.

Second pass on the clear-text gaps of R4840 and R4844 from the DECODE images (clear_gaps_pass2.md): 46 places, 32 read H/C, 8 M, 6 illegible; nine corrections to the working transcriptions (e.g. 'they are all borne under one planett', 'the ffrenche K.'), not yet merged into reading_R4840/R4844.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R4840 and R4844 linked to the working transcriptions with glossed numbers (reading_R48xx.txt) and the second-pass gap readings (clear_gaps_pass2.md); the R4844 sign words and the name-code table copied verbatim from NOTES.md into texts/. Missing: R4838 (28 Jul) and R4839 (7 Aug) were left to CSP Scotland viii nos. 40 and 65 and have no transcription in the folder

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): reading_R4840.txt and reading_R4844.txt read through. R4840 reads as English sentences with glossed name codes, its [..] being illegible clear text (reviewed B); R4844 has unread sign-alphabet words or open codes in nearly every sentence and is relabelled decoded, not read. fraction_read 0.49 -> 0.43 (units in letters that read).

Re-read of R4844 under REREAD_BRIEF (batch mix1): no decipherment, edition or calendar entry; DECODE images out of reach; the unmerged 14 Oct gap readings merged into reading_R4844_r2.txt (sentence check 0.45 -> 0.50). Sign words and open codes still in nearly every sentence: stays decoded, not read.

v6 spelling check (23 Oct 2026, research/reading_audit/v6_spelling_files.txt): reading_R4840.txt and reading_R4844_r2.txt ('spelling modernised in part'): DECODE images fetched again with the project cookie (research/reading_audit/v6_fetch.py, scratchpad only) and re-read in strips; the words whose letters are clear in the secretary hand respelt as written (dothe, complayne, wrytten, frende, knowe, countenaunce, yf, woold, ioyne, wyll, realme, iudge, then for than, Coorte, hathe bread, lykinge, doe bothe allowe of yt, untill, ben unmindfull, commyt ...); uncertain words keep the earlier form; no hole filled, no word changed. Rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py: reading_R4840.txt plain 0.409 -> 0.296, explicit holes 0.614 -> 0.667; reading_R4844_r2.txt plain 0.409 -> 0.226, explicit holes 0.705 -> 0.736. The plain share falls with period spelling against a modern word list; the explicit-hole share, the bar for period spelling, is unchanged or the change comes from the new header lines in files without a '## Reading' heading. No state changes.

Lead from research/patterns/DEEPER.md: Stafford's Walsingham cipher of 1586 (harley1582r8500/key.tsv) compared with the R4844 sign words. Only 35 of 131 signs (26%) have a Stafford sign label, and the frequent word-initial signs (□, ≠, ÷) are absent from that alphabet. Ruled out at the label level; a glyph-by-glyph check needs the R4844 images (DECODE login).

Sign alphabet learnt on the glossed sign words of the deciphered pairs DECODE R4689, R4835, R4836 (Add MS 32657); one pre-registered held-out test on R4845 (29 words, 178 letters, transcribed blind and glossed by separate agents): 0.646 vs best of 200 shuffled keys 0.213, partial; R4844 sign words read in part (16 of 19 groups); name codes 3 (the Queen / England, not France), 14 (Leicester), 27 (the Secretary), 37 (Scotland) from the pairs' glosses (dudout/README.md; Brice Dudout / Claude).

validation.notes: clear letters with about 40 two-digit name codes (one name each) and an unread 14-word sign run; no letter-level cipher reading to test

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The two-digit name code was rebuilt mainly from the bracketed glosses in CSP Scotland viii (1914) nos. 40, 41, 65, 106 (19 Arran, 24 Farnihurst, 39 Gray, 40 Justice Clerk, 20 Morton, 10 the King), supplemented by sense in Wotton's drafts R4841-R4843 in the same volume; the letters are otherwise in clear.

not glossed in CSP or Wotton drafts; context too thin
second pass 14 Oct 2026 (clear_gaps_pass2.md): 32 of 46 places read H/C, 8 M, 6 illegible (blots, stains, struck interlinear words)

outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: only letters that read count. Units as before (name-code occurrences, each sign-alphabet word one unit): R4840 20 and R4838/R4839 10 (code lists in NOTES) are in letters that read; R4844's 39 units (16 codes, 23 sign words) are decoded, not read. 30 of 69 = 0.43. Withdrawn as a reading figure: 0.49 (34 of 69 units read, pooled over both ciphers); per part as in outcome.parts.
outcome.notes: All four letters readable; two already in print as calendar abstracts. Name code mostly identified; the ~14 sign words of 10 Sep 1585 unread. fraction_read is a rough estimate from NOTES, not a count: name numbers mostly identified (6 of 16 open), the ~14 sign words of R4844 unread.

texts.label: R4840, Add MS 32657 ff. 163-164, the Court, 21 Aug 1585
texts.summary: Walsingham warns Edward Wotton, ambassador to James VI, that the Master of Gray [39] complains of Wotton's coldness and offers proof of his devotion if the banished lords join Maxwell [20] on the Borders, lest the King be carried away from England while the French party grows; Walsingham advises dealing warily with them all. The letter is clear English with a two-digit name code; clear_gaps_pass2.md holds the 14 Oct 2026 gap readings and nine corrections not yet merged.

reading_review.note: reading_R4840.txt reads as English sentences with the name codes glossed (39, the Master of Gray, complains of your countenance towards him ...; the King to be carried away from England; press the imprisonment of Farnihurst). The [..] are clear-text places illegible on the image, most resolved in clear_gaps_pass2.md, not cipher holes; two codes (27, 40) partly glossed. Audit grade C refined for R4840.

texts.label: R4844, Add MS 32657 ff. 194-195, the Court, 10 Sep 1585
texts.summary: Walsingham to Wotton on the articles set down by the Master of Gray, the banished lords and Arran, with about fourteen words in a separate sign alphabet that stay unread (Wotton's interlinear decipherment is blotted out); a postscript says a go-between [23] deals between the King and the Jesuits.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (texts/R4844_reread_log.md): no decipherment exists (Wotton’s interlinear one is blotted), CSP Scotland viii does not calendar the letter, and the DECODE images are behind the login and not in the checkout. The 14 Oct gap readings (clear_gaps_pass2.md) were merged into reading_R4844_r2.txt (_check_reading 0.45 -> 0.50), but every sentence of the body still carries a sign word (11 groups, about 120 signs, homophonic with nulls, no crib, no key: too short) or an open name code (13, 14, 23, 30, 32, 37). Fragments only.

texts.label: R4844 sign words read with the key from the deciphered pairs (Brice Dudout)
texts.summary: Walsingham to Wotton, 10 Sep 1585: the Master of Gray's plot is to be judged; the Queen will not make herself a party; no violent course; Wotton is to be absent at the attempt, keep his train at Stirling and avoid suspicion; a postscript on Lord Scrope's letter about the secret plot, not kept secret enough.
texts.note: 16 of 19 sign groups read, 3 unresolved; about 86% of the sign letters read for sense (about 84% without the 2 restored letters); key partial by our protocol (0.646 vs 0.213 on held-out R4845).

reading_review.note: the sign words read as words in the clear sentences of R4844; coherent but with three gaps and several probable words

prior.where: CSP Scotland viii (1914) nos. 40, 65 calendar two of the four letters from Walsingham's drafts; the calendar glosses 19, 24, 39, 40 and names 20 as Morton
